name: Turkey
summary_text: Turkey presents real, structured danger for trans visitors — institutionalised, presidential-level hostility that has become state policy. Police profile and detain trans women for identity checks (20 were detained in Istanbul in July 2025), trans women have historically been "frequent targets of torture and ill-treatment" by police, and a trans woman attacked with a knife was herself detained (victim-criminalised). A draft law leaked in October 2025 would criminalise LGBT people — not yet passed but under active government consideration. Transphobic attacks and Pride-event violence are documented, the Health Ministry is introducing regulations that may profile and restrict trans healthcare, and foreign visitors must carry original passports at all times — creating outing risk at the frequent transit checkpoints. If detained, trans women are placed in men's facilities with documented rights violations. The risk is concentrated in urban trans-visible contexts (Istanbul's Beyoğlu/Tarlabaşı) rather than package-holiday tourist zones, but the institutional hostility pervades. Turkey is outside the Schengen area.

sources.title: Türkiye: Draft Law Threatens LGBT People with Prison | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Oct 2025): 'Türkiye: Draft Law Threatens LGBT People with Prison' — a proposed penal-code package would effectively criminalise LGBT people with long prison terms.

Kaos GL (Feb 2026): 'A major siege' against LGBTI+ people in 2025 - hostility turned into state policy; the LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 ('The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People') documents institutionalised anti-LGBTI policies, hate speech from senior officials, and instructions to public institutions under the 'Year of the Family' banner creating a climate encouraging human-rights violations.

sources.title: İstanbul police detain trans women for ID checks amid profiling concerns
sources.claim_summary: bianet (Aug 2025): Istanbul police detain ~20 trans women for ID checks amid profiling concerns - stopped on the street, while shopping or in cafés in Beyoğlu, held at Taksim Şehit Haşim Usta Police Station and released after 'General Information Gathering' (GBT) background checks; legal experts argue GBT checks violate ECHR Article 5; one detainee: 'They didn't fine us, but they documented us. The new law hasn't even passed yet, but they're already enforcing it on us.'

sources.title: Report documents sharp rise in LGBTQ rights violations in Turkey in 2025 - Turkish Minute
sources.claim_summary: Turkish Minute (Feb 2026): report documents sharp rise in LGBTQ rights violations in Turkey in 2025 - coverage of the Kaos GL report findings.

sources.title: “You should have behaved yourseld!” - 2025 Istanbul Trans and LGBTI+ Pride Week Monitoring Report | Hafıza Merkezi
sources.claim_summary: Truth Justice Memory Center et al. (Aug 2025): 'You should have behaved yourself!' - 2025 Istanbul Trans and LGBTI+ Pride Week monitoring report by seven human-rights organisations documenting violations during and after the 11th Trans Pride March and 23rd Istanbul LGBTI+ Pride March; systematic violations ongoing since 2015, with senior officials using discriminatory rhetoric.

sources.title: Turkey: New Health Ministry regulation may profile trans people and restrict transition access
sources.claim_summary: Kaos GL (Sept 2025): a new Health Ministry regulation may profile trans people and restrict transition access - 'gender reassignment' added to official reasons for medical board reports; e-reports replace paper; boards must now include six specialities examining applicants separately; the ministry says it 'does not grant a new right' but strengthens 'control and monitoring mechanisms'.

sources.title: Transphobic attack in Istanbul
sources.claim_summary: Kaos GL (Aug 2024): transphobic attack in Istanbul - trans woman Yaşam was attacked with a knife by a 17-year-old in Bakırköy; the victim was detained and spent the night in a detention centre while the attacker was released; 'The detention of the victim trans woman, not the knife attacker, reveals the hate policy of the Turkish state.'

sources.title: Turkey Passport Rules: 2026 Fines & Detention Warning
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (timeout); the underlying Nomad Lawyer piece (2026) covers Turkey's passport-carrying rule, fines and detention warnings.

sources.title: Turkey: Homophobic Violence Points to Rights Crisis | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (May 2008): launch of the 123-page report 'We Need a Law for Liberation' — documents a long, continuing history of violence and abuse based on sexual orientation and gender identity and calls for legal reform, urging the EU to tie membership prospects to ending the abuses.
